title: Steak and Kidney Pudding
subtitle: British steamed suet pudding with beef and kidney filling
excerpt: Steak and kidney pudding is one of the great dishes of English cooking: a tender suet pastry crust steamed for several hours, enclosing a filling of beef, kidney, and a rich, thick gravy. When the pudding is cut open at the table, the gravy steams out. It is old-fashioned, substantial, and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Steak and kidney pudding is one of the most ancient dishes in English cooking. Beefsteak and kidney pudding was being made in the 18th century. The suet crust is the same pastry used for spotted dick, treacle pudding, and other steamed puddings. It is one of the most distinctively English forms of cooking -- the long steam in the pudding basin produces a crust that is soft, dense, and entirely different from a baked pastry.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made a day ahead. Assemble and steam the day of serving.

content.text: The filling goes in raw or just briefly browned -- it finishes cooking during the long steam. A 1.2 litre pudding basin is needed. The pudding steams for 4 hours in a pan of simmering water -- the water must be kept topped up throughout. Do not let the pan run dry.

items.prepNote: tough core removed, cut into 2 cm pieces

content.text: Make the suet pastry: mix {{plain-flour}} flour, {{suet-shredded}} suet, {{baking-powder}} baking powder, and {{salt-table}} salt. Add cold water a tablespoon at a time until a soft dough forms (about 150 ml). Do not overwork. Roll out two-thirds on a floured surface and use to line a greased 1.2-litre pudding basin, leaving an overhang.

Toss {{beef-chuck}} beef and {{ox-kidney}} kidney in {{plain-flour}} seasoned flour with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Mix with {{onion}} onion, {{thyme-fresh}} thyme, and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Pack into the pastry-lined basin. Pour in {{beef-stock}} stock and {{worcestershire-sauce}} Worcestershire sauce.

Roll out the remaining pastry for the lid. Press onto the filling, pinch the edges to seal, and trim the overhang. Cover with a double layer of pleated foil (the pleat allows for expansion). Tie with string to secure. Lower into a large pot of simmering water (the water should come halfway up the basin). Cover and steam for 4 hours, checking and topping up the water every 30 minutes. Turn out onto a plate and serve at the table.

items.symptom: The suet pastry is heavy and dense
items.cause: Overworked, or too much water added at once.
items.fix: Suet pastry should be mixed briefly until just combined -- it needs much less handling than butter pastry. Add the water cautiously: stop as soon as the dough comes together.

content.text: Steak and kidney pudding is one of the most English of dishes. It appears in Victorian literature and in 19th-century cookbooks. It remains on the menu of traditional British restaurants and pubs. It is a dish of winter and of formal Sunday cooking. The suet crust tradition links it to dozens of other steamed and boiled British puddings, both savoury and sweet.
